articles.title: 10 rules for living longer, seeing your grandkids grow up and enjoying your retirement savings
articles.summary: Dr. Michael Hall shares his 10 basic longevity rules for healthy aging, from sleep and movement to purpose and social connection, in his new book.
articles.body: As scientists increasingly investigate how everyday habits may influence health and aging, one longevity doctor says the keys to a longer, healthier life don't require expensive supplements, elaborate biohacks or cutting-edge treatments. Dr. Michael Hall, a Miami Beach longevity physician and author of the new book, "Infinite Youth," has identified what he calls the "10 commandments of longevity," which he believes can help people extend their healthiest years. Hall said the principles were shaped by nearly two decades in longevity medicine and by observing health and aging across cultures around the world. LONGEVITY DOCTOR REVEALS WHAT MATTERS MOST FOR AGING WELL, BEYOND PRICEY BIOHACKS "These are core elements that are not peptides, they're not NAD," Hall told Fox News Digital. "It's not that you've got to buy a fancy thing on Amazon." Instead, he said, "you start out with the basics and you maintain them consistently." "If you’re embracing some of these things, you are doing exactly what you need to do — and these don’t cost anything." No. 1: Guard your attention The content that people repeatedly consume — particularly when it’s fear-based or negative — can shape their behavior, according to Hall. He sees protecting attention as part of protecting health, emphasizing the importance of being intentional about what people consume mentally. "What you put in your mind, you need to be very careful about," he said. "What you think, you become." ONE SIMPLE LIFESTYLE CHOICE COULD HELP YOU LIVE LONGER, SAYS LONGEVITY EXPERT No. 2: Honor sleep A recent study identified a "sweet spot" of about six to eight hours of sleep per day, which researchers linked to healthier aging and lower risks of premature death and disease. Sleep is when the body recovers and the brain "resets," yet technology and poor sleep habits increasingly interfere with that process, according to Hall. "Sleep is probably one of the most important things that we just don’t talk about enough," he said. The expert pointed out that the body’s circadian rhythm responds naturally to light and darkness, while screens, artificial light and late bedtimes can disrupt that cycle. "The bed is really for sleep and sex," Hall added. No. 3: Move daily A September 2026 study found that highly active older adults maintained high levels of aerobic fitness into their 60s, 70s and 80s, despite some normal age-related decline. "Movement is life," Hall agreed. He recalled seeing older adults remain highly active during his time working in New Zealand and Sri Lanka, including women in their 90s who were still mobile and fit. 3 COMMON FACTORS MAY BE SECRETLY SPEEDING UP THE AGING PROCESS, EXPERT SAYS Hall’s own routine includes walking, swimming, cycling and resistance work. For everyday movement, he particularly recommends walking and squatting, which engage large muscle groups and help maintain strength and mobility. No. 4: Preserve strength Muscle strength helps support bones, posture and mobility, and may help reduce frailty and fall risk later in life, according to the longevity expert. "You need to maintain that good, healthy posture and strength throughout your life," Hall said. He connected loss of movement and strength with weakening muscles, bones, tendons and ligaments, potentially increasing fall risk as people age. "If you’re moving, you’re preserving strength, you’re maintaining your bones, because they go together," Hall said. No. 5: Eat real food For optimal longevity nutrition, Hall recommends choosing minimally processed foods, with a focus on simple preparation, portion control and awareness of what goes into meals. "Food is medicine, food is fuel, food is life," Hall said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER While Hall said he cooks his own meals, primarily chooses fresh foods and largely avoids foods that come "out of a bag or a box," he emphasizes portion control rather than complete deprivation. "I don’t care what it is you love, you can have a bite," he said. No. 6: Embrace purpose Having a mission gives people something beyond themselves to invest in, contributing to emotional well-being and a meaningful life, according to Hall. "It’s the most important part of being human," he said. "Our mission … is our purpose." That purpose does not have to come from an extraordinary calling, Hall suggested. Whether someone is a physician, firefighter, baker or coffee shop owner, serving others can provide a sense of meaning. "If you’re just serving yourself, you aren’t going to be a happy person," he added. No. 7: Cultivate meaningful relationships "No one ages well alone," Hall said. "You cannot live alone. You’re not designed to be atomized living in a box alone." Research published in October 2026 in PLOS One found that loneliness was associated with a higher risk of death at one, three and five years. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Hall also pointed to companionship, family and meaningful relationships as important parts of his own life. "Having people around you who appreciate you, who you can relate to, who can have a conversation with, have a laugh with, it’s so important," he said. No. 8: Welcome challenge A 2025 study of more than 10,000 older adults with cognitive impairment found that greater participation in cognitively stimulating activities was associated with a lower risk of death over time. "We’re needing to be challenged … as an individual and as a community and as society," Hall said. No. 9: Remain curious Continuing to learn, explore and seek out new experiences could play a role in healthy aging, research has found. Hall similarly believes curiosity helps people remain engaged with the world as they get older. "Curiosity allows us to explore and to always be aware there’s something more," he told Fox News Digital. "You’re never going to know everything. So you’re always on the quest." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Curiosity has driven much of Hall’s travel and work around the world, he said, noting that getting older shouldn't mean stopping the pursuit of new experiences. "We were children, and we never really grew up, by the way — we just get older in our bodies." No. 10: Keep the funnel wide In his book, Hall describes healthy aging as keeping the body's metaphorical "funnel" as wide as possible for as long as possible. He sees aging as a gradual narrowing of that funnel, with increasing physiological stress as the body loses some of its ability to maintain optimal function. "We were children, and we never really grew up — we just get older in our bodies." Keeping the funnel wide, he said, means supporting overall health and resilience through the fundamental habits outlined in his other commandments. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Ultimately, Hall said his goal is not simply to help people accumulate more birthdays, but to make those additional years healthier and more meaningful. "I’m selling healthspan as much as I possibly can," he said. "Your best years of your life, the best living you can possibly have, sharing with others and making society better."

articles.title: Dr Drew Pinsky likens smartphones to a 'crack pipe' in warning over behavioral addictions
articles.summary: Dr. Drew Pinsky compared smartphones to a "crack pipe," warning that gambling addiction and sex addiction are now right at everyone's fingertips.
articles.body: Dr. Drew Pinsky compared the smartphone in your pocket to a "crack pipe" while warning that these devices place gambling and sexual behavior in the palm of your hand on Tuesday's episode of "Hang Out with Sean Hannity." "I want you to think gambling and sex in the same thought," he said. "It's really on right now, those two behavioral addictions." But these addictive behaviors aren't one-size-fits-all. Gamblers, he said, come in "several different flavors." ‘ADDICTION ECONOMY’ IS A BAD GAMBLE FOR YOUNG MEN. HERE’S THEIR WAY OUT "One is the guys that like to win. That's what we think of with gambling addiction. That's not most of them. Most of them like to lose," said Pinsky. "They don't feel alive unless their back is against the wall. And then there's sociopathic gambling, which is they just like to manipulate the system and find a way to win." As for sex addiction, Pinsky called it a "big problem now, growing fast," pointing to pornography as a major part of the issue. He also defended group-based recovery programs, saying communities of recovering addicts tend to police themselves and treat sexual relationships between participants as a serious threat to recovery. BRYCE HARPER VIDEO TO FANDUEL USER WITH GAMBLING ADDICTION UNDER REVIEW BY PENNSYLVANIA OFFICIALS Pinsky added that alcoholism is "mixed in" with the behavioral addictions he described. The doctor's warning comes as recent research points to shifts in drinking habits among Americans. New data shows that drinking in the U.S. has declined for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic. But overall alcohol use still remains above pre-pandemic levels, with one particular group showing a sharp increase in heavy intake. A study led by the University of Southern California/Keck Medicine found that among adults ages 50 to 64, alcohol use increased by nearly 4% from 2018 to 2024, while heavy drinking increased by more than 36%. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Across all age groups, alcohol use declined by nearly 2%, and heavy drinking declined by more than 8% from 2022 to 2024. Among Gen Z adults, alcohol use declined by more than 5%. Millennials drank approximately 17% less from 2022 to 2024. articles.title: Semi-synthetic kratom products linked to four deaths in Utah, state officials say
articles.summary: Four deaths in Utah have been linked to potent semi-synthetic kratom compounds, state officials said Monday.
articles.body: Four deaths in Utah have been linked to potent semi-synthetic kratom compounds, state officials said Monday. The kratom-derived compounds, mitragynine pseudoindoxyl (MGPI) and dihydro-7-hydroxymitragynine (MGM-15), are illegal in the state and were recently classified by the Drug Enforcement Administration as Schedule 1 drugs. Both are semi-synthetic derivatives of kratom. Utah health, poison center and agriculture officials warned that the compounds were found in certain herbal supplements, including kratom products, as well as products labeled “cat’s claw.” Cat’s claw is not a harmful supplement, but testing in these cases revealed it contained MPGI and MGM-15, the statement said. The warning said that the products were “often sold under brand names like ‘Buzzers’ and are misleadingly labeled as containing ‘cat’s claw’ or its scientific name Uncaria tomentosa.” The labels, officials said, often claim the product is “legal and free of kratom, yet warn it is for ‘adults only/21+’ or produces strong psychoactive effects.” Dr. Michael Moss, the medical director of the Utah Poison Control Center, said one of the four deaths was linked to a Buzzers product. “These cat’s claw products contain dangerous opioids derived from kratom,” Moss said. “No one should take these products, retailers should not sell them, and healthcare providers should be aware of potential for addiction, withdrawal, and overdose related to their use.” Experts say that cat’s claw, which comes from a South American vine, is generally safe. It’s taken by some people for its anti-inflammatory properties. Kratom is used for pain relief, depression and opioid withdrawal but is highly addictive and can cause overdose and death in extreme cases. Neither are approved by the Food and Drug Administration. The agency says kratom is not appropriate for use as a dietary supplement. Exo Club, which makes Buzzers, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. On its website, it says the product does not contain kratom. “We extract an indole alkaloid from the Cat’s Claw plant to mirror the effects of popular kratom products,” the website reads. In recent months, Utah has noticed calls to poison control about cat’s claw products, which experts say do not cause harmful side effects. People were instead reporting symptoms that resemble an opioid overdose, Moss previously told NBC News. Several other states have also recently issued warnings about products labeled to be cat’s claw but contained compounds related to kratom. Tennessee issued its own warning in September after the state’s Bureau of Investigation found the synthetic kratom compound MGM-15 in cat’s claw products. In Virginia, the Blue Ridge Poison Center has also received calls about cat’s claw products that caused opioid-like effects. Kratom is banned in at least 10 states, and many others regulate it or have bans on specific kratom-related compounds. Last year, the FDA recommended the Justice Department classify 7-hydroxymitragynine, or 7-OH, an opioid found in the kratom plant, as an illicit substance. This summer, the DEA announced its intent to do so, but has not yet done so. It has, however, temporarily classified several other kratom-related compounds, including MGPI and MGM-15, as Schedule 1 drugs. According to a report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 233 deaths were linked to kratom from 2015 to 2025. TMZ reported that, according to the medical examiner’s office in Nashville, Tennessee, Grammy-nominated record producer Tay Keith, 29, whose real name was BryTavious Chambers, had a kratom chemical and ketamine in his system when he was found dead in June. In 2023, the family of a Florida woman was awarded $11 million in a wrongful death lawsuit after the coroner attributed her death to “acute mitragynine intoxication,” referring to a compound found in kratom. In Mississippi, investigators are looking into the deaths of two University of Mississippi students in September. Packaged kratom was found at the scene of both deaths.

articles.title: The No. 1 Plant-Based Protein to Lower Cholesterol, According to a Dietitian
articles.summary: High cholesterol can sneak up on you, but making smart food choices can add up. Look for these plant proteins to get healthy fiber every day, a dietitian says.
articles.body: High cholesterol has a way of sneaking up on you. But, by focusing on what you put on your plate, those small choices can add up to big improvements in cholesterol numbers. While experts now agree that cholesterol in our food doesn’t directly impact cholesterol levels in blood, food choices still matter. And by opting for the right high-protein plant foods, you can make a significant impact on your cholesterol levels. In particular, look for plant proteins with fiber — especially soluble fiber, says Natalie Rizzo, registered dietitian and TODAY nutrition editor. “Soluble fiber binds to cholesterol and bile acids in the digestive tract, and removes them from the body with stool,” she explains. “Over time, eating the recommended amount of daily fiber can help lower LDL, or ‘bad,’ cholesterol.” You can find fiber, including soluble fiber, in many types of plant foods, including fruit, vegetables, whole grains and legumes. The No. 1 Plant-Based Protein to Help Lower Cholesterol Beans Beans are Rizzo’s top choice because they’re “an excellent combination of plant-based protein and soluble fiber,” she says. “That soluble fiber is particularly helpful for lowering LDL cholesterol.” The beans with the most fiber are navy beans, which provide more than 9 grams of fiber per serving, TODAY.com explained previously. Black beans and red adzuki beans are just behind that, each containing around 8 grams of fiber per serving. Beans are packed with filling protein as well as gut- and heart-healthy fiber. Plus, they’re affordable, versatile and easy to keep on-hand, Rizzo says. She likes to use them in quesadillas and tacos. You can also easily blend white beans into soups, dips and sauces for an added kick of fiber and plant protein. Other Plant Proteins to Manage Cholesterol Levels Lentils Another star legume, lentils provide a healthy dose of fiber alongside plant protein. A half-cup serving of lentils will net you 9 grams of protein as well as 8 grams of fiber. “They’re also naturally very low in saturated fat,” Rizzo says. “I especially like lentils because they cook relatively quickly and can easily replace some or all of the meat in a recipe.” Lentils are, of course, excellent in soups and curries, Rizzo says, but she also likes to add them to salads and pasta sauces. Nuts Fiber is the star when it comes to lowering cholesterol, but heart-healthy unsaturated fats are an important component of your diet, too, Rizzo says. “Replacing foods high in saturated fat with foods rich in unsaturated fats can help lower LDL cholesterol,” explains Rizzo. She recommends nuts, especially almonds and walnuts, because “they can replace foods higher in saturated fat, like nut butter instead of butter on toast,” she says. “They’re calorie-dense, but that doesn’t mean you need to avoid them. A handful handful of nuts is generally a satisfying serving,” she adds. Rizzo loves to add nuts to oatmeal, yogurt and salads, or snack on them on their own. She’s also a fan of nut butters on toast, in smoothies or with fruit. “They’re an easy way to add protein and heart-healthy fats without having to cook anything,” she says.

articles.title: Two candidates die during police constable recruitment run, heart attack suspected
articles.summary: Two UP Police constable candidates collapsed during a 4.8km physical test in Ghaziabad and died in hospital; heart attack suspected, autopsy awaited.
articles.body: GHAZIABAD: Two candidates appearing for the physical round of the UP Police constable recruitment drive, underway at the 47th Battalion PAC ground in Govindpuram from Oct 3, collapsed and died in hospital this week.On Tuesday, Vivek Kumar (23) of Shamli collapsed while running during the physical test and was declared dead at Joint District Hospital in Sanjay Nagar. On Monday, 27-year-old Atul Kumar from Mathura fainted during the run and was taken to Joint District Hospital. He was later referred to Safdarjung Hospital but died during treatment. While police suspect the two candidates suffered a heart attack, their bodies have been sent for autopsy and the reports are awaited.Vivek’s father, Balendra Rana, said officials conducting the recruitment had told them that his son had completed six of the nine rounds when he lost consciousness and collapsed. “When he regained consciousness, he stood up while leaning onto a pole and again started to run. He again stumbled and collapsed to the ground,” Rana said, adding that doctors cited heart failure as the cause of his death.According to his family, Vivek had scored 266 marks in the police recruitment exam. He had left home on Monday morning with a cousin, booked a hotel room in Ghaziabad and reached the ground to take the physical test on Tuesday morning. “Vivek was my only son. He was a volleyball player and trained regularly at Gorakhpur Sports College. I am a farmer and have 15 bighas of land. All I wanted was to see my son in a police uniform,” he said.DCP (headquarters) Balwant Kumar Chaudhary told TOI that for the constable recruitment exam, the two candidates had to complete a 4.8km run. “Male applicants have to complete a 4.8-kilometre run within 24 minutes, while female applicants must complete 2.4 kilometres within 14 minutes. Candidates failing to finish within the stipulated time are disqualified,” the DCP said. The physical tests precede the medical examinations.According to officials, on each day of the seven-day drive, 875 candidates were called in around 5 am for the physical tests, which are over by 8 am. “Male candidates are divided into batches and, after formalities, their chest and height are measured before they take the physical test. articles.title: Alan Alda reveals unexpected weapon in his battle against Parkinson's disease
articles.summary: Alan Alda, now 90, reveals how humor and acceptance help him cope with Parkinson's disease, calling the condition "just a hobby" he lives with.
articles.body: Alan Alda is sharing his surprising method of coping with Parkinson’s. The actor, 90, best known for portraying Captain Benjamin Franklin "Hawkeye" Pierce in the CBS wartime sitcom "M*A*S*H," was diagnosed with the degenerative motor disease in 2015 and publicly shared the news in 2018. The diagnosis came after the actor learned that his own behavior of acting out dreams could be an early Parkinson's symptom. DAD JOKES MAY BE GOOD FOR YOUR BRAIN IN ONE SURPRISING WAY, EXPERTS SAY "I had a symptom, which at the time was not that well-known: Acting out your dreams," he said in an Oct. 4 interview with CBS News. "I had a dream that somebody was attacking me. And I picked up a sack of potatoes and threw it at 'em. What I was really doing was throwing a pillow at Arlene, my wife." Alda identified humor as his way of coping with the frustrations and limitations of the disease. While he acknowledged the frustrations of the physical effects and limitations of Parkinson’s, he said "the best way to deal with anything that's a little bit of a problem is to find out what's funny about it and laugh at it." In one example, he shared that when he has trouble controlling the computer mouse while composing an email, he personifies his condition as "Dr. Parkinson," moving his hand all over the screen and deleting things. "I don't let Parkinson's define me," Alda said, joking that he sees the disease as "just a hobby." PARKINSON’S PATIENT’S YEARS-LONG TREMOR VANISHES WITHIN MINUTES OF NEW ULTRASOUND TREATMENT Rather than wishing he didn’t have the condition, the actor said he aims to accept his current reality. "I really think reality is my friend," he said. "I don't want to wish it away. I can't wish it away. I can't hope for a better future. I gotta accept what is." Although Alda acknowledged that everyday tasks, such as buttoning his shirt, have become difficult, he said he treats each one like a "puzzle" to solve. "I do hate it, but the only thing that's helpful is: What haven't I tried? And pretty soon, you get the feeling, 'If I keep looking for new ways to try this, I'll get a solution.' It's a puzzle. Will I be able eventually to put my socks on? The last time I put my socks on was a tremendous moment to celebrate!" SCIENTISTS REVEAL SURPRISING BRAIN BENEFIT OF LAUGHTER: 'IT'S A MENTAL WORKOUT' Dr. Chadrick Lane, a neuropsychiatrist and director of the geriatric and neuropsychiatry clinic at UT Southwestern Medical Center in Dallas, Texas, agreed that humor can be a helpful wellness tool for those navigating the Parkinson's journey. "Humor involves cognitive reframing, this idea of looking at a circumstance through different angles — not necessarily changing the reality that one is in, but shifting the meaning and the emotional weight of the situation," Lane, who has not treated Alda, told Fox News Digital. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER When something feels frightening or distressing, such as a medical diagnosis, creating some "psychological distance" can make a "big, big change" in perspective, he added. Connection is another important component of humor, Lane noted. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "Humor is often shared. It brings us together," he said. "We are meant to share our lives with others. The importance of having a sense of belonging and humor can be a glue in that way, bringing us closer with others so that one does not go on the journey alone." "Humor is often shared. It brings us together." Lane shared that he has witnessed the power of humor and connection in his own practice as he cares for people living with Parkinson's disease. "One of the wonderful things that I've seen in those settings is that, just like Mr. Alda, people crack a joke, [it] brings them a smile." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The neuropsychiatrist also noted that Alda’s acceptance of his condition is "enormously empowering." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "It's the idea of saying to oneself, what are the choices that I can make in the moment?" Lane told Fox News Digital. "Rarely do we ever have control over our entire day and certainly not our entire life, but we often do have control over what we choose in the moment." "Our sense of agency is an important part of our emotional well-being."

articles.title: Southern California surfers are being diagnosed with a bizarre ‘tumor’ condition
articles.summary: Surfers have long braved shark bites, reef scrapes, and the dreaded "surfer's ear."
articles.body:
Surfers have long braved shark bites, reef scrapes, and the dreaded " surfer's ear ."

But now, aging wave-riders may be taking home a bizarre souvenir from years spent in the surf: strange, fatty growths bulging from their chests.

Doctors have identified the unusual lumps, called "liposurfomas," in longtime surfers, who appear to develop them after years of repeatedly grinding their torsos against hard surfboards while paddling out. While the alarming masses can look like tumors, researchers say they appear to be benign — although they can grow larger with continued surfing.

The peculiar condition has caught renewed attention in Southern California after researchers at the University of California, Irvine studied seven surfers with the distinctive growths. Dr. Jeffrey Klein, a dermatology professor at UC Irvine and one of the researchers behind the study, said the growths can be mistaken for cancer — potentially sending otherwise healthy surfers down a nerve-racking path of testing and treatment.

"These lesions are rather common in surfers," researchers wrote, noting that most surfers know somebody with the telltale soft, symmetrical chest bumps.

The masses are believed to result from "incessant low-intensity traumatic compression of subcutaneous tissue, squeezed between the costal margin and the hard deck of a surfboard while paddling in the prone position."

The growths are different from the better-known "surfer's knots," researchers say, which are hard, callus-like masses typically found on knees, feet, and shins of longboarders. Both are reportedly benign tissue growths.

Surf icon Corky Carroll even went public about his bulging torso in a 2010 column , referring to himself as "the man with four breasts."

The growths tend to swell during peak surf seasons and shrink slightly when surfers take extended time just on dry land. For surfers keen to ditch the extra set of pecs, treatments range from adding extra padding to wetsuits to surgical removal and liposuction.

However, doctors warn that if riders keep hitting the surf, the lumps can come right back.

articles.title: Patient falls from hospital’s 2nd floor, dies; probe ordered
articles.summary: 60-year-old liver patient dies after falling from 2nd floor at Maharshi Devraha Baba Medical College, Deoria; district panel probes accident vs jump.
articles.body: Lucknow: A 60-year-old patient undergoing treatment for a liver ailment at Maharshi Devraha Baba Medical College in Deoria died after falling from the second floor of the hospital building on Sunday night. The district administration has ordered an inquiry by a three-member team.The deceased, Ramanuj Chouhan, a resident of Bihar’s Gopalganj district, had been admitted to the medical ward on Friday. Hospital authorities said the incident occurred around 10pm when he went towards a corridor and fell from the second floor under mysterious circumstances.The fall left Ramanuj with severe injuries to his head, arms and legs. Hospital staff rushed him to the trauma centre, while principal Rajni Patel, CMS HK Mishra and a team of specialists reached the spot to supervise his treatment. A CT scan was conducted, and doctors later advised shifting him to Gorakhpur Medical College due to his critical condition. However, his family reportedly declined the referral, citing financial constraints. He died during treatment.District magistrate Madhusudan Hulgi constituted a three-member panel headed by Sadar Tehsildar Alka Singh to investigate whether Ramanuj accidentally fell while moving through the corridor or deliberately jumped from a window.According to CMS HK Mishra, Ramanuj’s wife and daughter-in-law had taken him towards the corridor shortly before the incident, possibly for a walk or to use the washroom. They raised an alarm after the fall, and hospital employees found him lying below. articles.title: People who live to 100 have 3 drinks in common, longevity expert says
articles.summary: Dan Buettner highlights how blue zones residents drink water, black coffee and red wine with resveratrol to support long-term health goals.
articles.body: In the world’s "blue zones" — regions such as Sardinia, Italy, and Okinawa, Japan, known for unusually high concentrations of long-lived residents — researchers have studied dietary and lifestyle habits for clues to healthy aging and longevity. In a recent video post, longevity researcher Dan Buettner highlighted three beverages commonly consumed in blue zones — and studies offer some clues about how each may affect health and longevity. No. 1: Purified water Buettner ranked water first among his three longevity drinks. FILTERED WATER AT SPECIFIC AGES COULD ADD MONTHS TO YOUR LIFESPAN DECADES LATER, NEW STUDY FINDS "The indisputable, best thing you can drink to live to 100 [is] water," he stated. "People in blue zones are drinking six to seven glasses of water. You want to make sure it is purified water. Water helps lower your blood pressure, helps keep your blood thin and keeps you hydrated." Research from the National Institutes of Health has linked better hydration with healthier aging, including lower risks of chronic disease and premature death, although researchers noted that the findings do not prove cause and effect. Other health experts note that adequate water intake supports kidney function, helps regulate blood pressure and keeps blood circulating effectively. No. 2: Black coffee Coffee consumption is another daily habit highlighted by Buettner, who said it is associated with lower rates of diabetes and Parkinson's. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "Drink it black, one to two cups a day, quit by noon, it'll help you live longer," he added. Coffee contains antioxidants and polyphenols, plant compounds that have been studied for their potential anti-inflammatory effects. Routine coffee consumption has also been associated with lower risks of type 2 diabetes and neurological conditions. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Limiting added sugars and heavy creams can help avoid extra calories, while consuming caffeine earlier in the day may reduce its impact on sleep. No. 3: Red wine Residents in blue zone areas, like Sardinia, often consume small amounts of red wine during meals. Buettner acknowledged that red wine's place in a longevity-focused diet is "controversial." "I'm very well aware of all the negative press wine is getting lately, but it's consumed in the blue zones and it seems to add years to life." Red wine contains plant compounds such as resveratrol and flavonoids, which have been studied for their potential cardiovascular effects. However, experts have increasingly questioned whether any benefits attributed to red wine outweigh the known risks of alcohol. articles.title: Sobrinha de Rainha de Rodeio morta por raio recebeu descarga elétrica | G1
articles.standfirst: Ana Beatriz estava penteando o cabelo da sobrinha quando as duas foram atingidas. Menina de oito anos foi hospitalizada, passou por exames e recebeu alta, segundo família.
articles.summary: Ana Beatriz  estava penteando o cabelo da sobrinha quando as duas foram atingidas. Menina de oito anos foi hospitalizada, passou por exames e recebeu alta, segundo família.
articles.body:
A sobrinha da Rainha de Rodeio Ana Beatriz Araújo, de 22 anos, ficou algumas horas sem sentir as pernas após também ser atingida por uma descarga elétrica que matou a tia, em Almas, na região sudeste do Tocantins. As duas estavam em uma área no fundo de uma casa quando foram atingidas pela descarga elétrica durante uma chuva leve, na tarde de sábado (3).

📱 Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 TO no WhatsApp

Segundo Lana Letícia, irmã da jovem, Ana Beatriz estava penteando o cabelo da sobrinha de 8 anos depois de dar banho nela quando recebeu a descarga. As duas caíram no chão. "Ninguém imagina que aquela chuva leve ia acontecer isso."

De acordo com Lana, a sobrinha acordou logo após a descarga, mas ficou algumas horas sem sentir as pernas. Ela foi levada para atendimento no Hospital Regional de Dianópolis, onde passou uma noite internada e fez exames.

Alguns exames apresentaram alterações e foram repetidos. Após nova avaliação, a menina recebeu alta na tarde de domingo (4). Segundo a família, a criança está bem e a dormência na perna passou.

A descarga atingiu Ana Beatriz por completo, segundo a irmã. Ela chegou a ser reanimada depois de perder os batimentos cardíacos, mas não recuperou a consciência.

Ainda conforme Lana, a jovem teve outras paradas cardíacas durante o trajeto até uma unidade de saúde em Porto Nacional, a cerca de 230 km de Almas. Ela não resistiu.

O acidente aconteceu por volta das 15h. Segundo a família, o sábado havia começado nublado e a chuva começou à tarde, mas o tempo não aparentava oferecer risco.

Na casa da mãe de Ana Beatriz havia uma pequena área no fundo, um tanque de lavar roupas e várias árvores. A jovem havia acabado de dar banho no próprio filho antes de ficar com a sobrinha.

Ana Beatriz havia completado 22 anos no dia 26 de setembro, uma semana antes do acidente. Conhecida na cidade e pela família pelo apelido carinhoso de "Aninha", a jovem foi eleita Rainha de Rodeio na 27ª edição da ExpoAlmas 2026 e havia ingressado recentemente no curso de Fisioterapia.

Segundo Lana, a jovem gostava de musculação, cuidava da alimentação e gostava de estar sempre arrumada. Também gostava de fazer receitas e era conhecida pelo jeito brincalhão e pelo “gênio forte”.

“Ela tinha seu jeito único de ser”, contou a irmã. Ana Beatriz foi sepultada nesta segunda-feira (5), em Almas. Na mesma data em que a irmã, Lana completou 24 anos.

articles.title: Acúmulo de santinhos após votação resulta em recolhimento de meia tonelada de papel em Pouso Alegre, MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Derramamento de propaganda eleitoral é considerado crime e provocou sujeira e riscos em diferentes pontos da cidade; uma idosa de 85 anos ficou ferida após escorregar nos papéis.
articles.summary: Derramamento de propaganda eleitoral é considerado crime e provocou sujeira e riscos em diferentes pontos da cidade; uma idosa de 85 anos ficou ferida após escorregar nos papéis.
articles.body:
Cerca de 500 quilos de santinhos de propaganda eleitoral foram recolhidos das ruas de Pouso Alegre (MG) após a votação do último domingo. De acordo com a prefeitura, o volume retirado das vias públicas chegou a meia tonelada e evidencia o impacto do descarte irregular de material de campanha na cidade.

Mesmo dias após as eleições, ainda era possível encontrar santinhos espalhados em ruas próximas a locais de votação. Além da sujeira e da poluição visual, o material representou risco para pedestres.

Acúmulo de santinhos após votação resulta em recolhimento de meia tonelada de papel em Pouso Alegre (MG) — Foto: Iago Almeida

Um dos casos mais graves foi registrado em frente à Escola Estadual Vinícius Meyer, no bairro São Geraldo, considerada a maior seção eleitoral do município. No local, uma idosa de 85 anos escorregou nos santinhos espalhados pela calçada enquanto caminhava para a missa.

Ela foi socorrida pelo Corpo de Bombeiros e encaminhada ao Hospital Samuel Libânio. Segundo a aposentada, a haste de seus óculos atingiu a região do supercílio durante a queda. Após receber atendimento médico e permanecer em observação, ela foi liberada e segue a recuperação em casa.

Idosa ficou ferida após escorregar em santinhos e cair na calçada — Foto: Iago Almeida

A legislação eleitoral considera crime o derramamento de santinhos em vias públicas, especialmente nas proximidades dos locais de votação.

Além de quem realiza a distribuição do material, o próprio candidato pode ser responsabilizado. A multa prevista para a infração varia de R$ 2 mil a R$ 8 mil.

A Prefeitura de Pouso Alegre informou que reforçou os serviços de limpeza após o pleito e que o monitoramento continuará durante as próximas etapas do processo eleitoral.

articles.title: Indígena de18 anos morre eletrocutado enquanto colhia mangas no Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: Jovem usou uma barra de ferro que tocou na fiação de alta tensão. Bombeiros precisaram acionar a Energisa para desligar a rede e retirar o corpo.
articles.summary: Jovem usou uma barra de ferro que tocou na fiação de alta tensão. Bombeiros precisaram acionar a Energisa para desligar a rede e retirar o corpo.
articles.body:
O adolescente indígena Elissandro Bilo Macário Kaxinawá, de 18 anos, morreu após sofrer uma descarga elétrica enquanto colhia mangas no bairro Miritizal, em Cruzeiro do Sul , no interior do Acre, nesta quarta-feira (7).

José Matheus Kaxinawá, tio-avô, testemunhou o incidente e descreveu o momento. Ele disse que a família havia almoçado junta e pediu autorização a um vizinho para pegar as frutas.

"Ele permitiu e meu sobrinho resolveu subir. Só que ele acertou o lado errado, o ferro tocou na fiação elétrica e resultou nesse acidente", lamentou.

O Corpo de Bombeiros foi acionado, mas, ao chegar ao local, já encontrou o jovem sem vida. De acordo com o coordenador de desastres da Defesa Civil, subtenente Iranilson Neri, a vítima permaneceu presa ao cabo de alta tensão após o choque.

Elissandro Bilo Macário Kaxinawá, de 18 anos, morreu eletrocutado em Cruzeiro do Sul — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

"Ao chegarmos ao local, verificamos que a vítima realmente estava no pé de manga e havia também uma barra de ferro grudada à vítima e na fiação de alta tensão, precisando de uma mobilização maior para tirá-lo", explicou.

Por causa do risco de uma nova descarga, a equipe acionou a concessionária Energisa para fazer o desligamento da rede na região.

Após a interrupção, os bombeiros subiram na arvore e removeram o corpo.

O acidente também assustou uma pessoa que passava pelo local no momento da descarga elétrica. A Rede Amazônica conversou com a testemunha, identificada apenas como Rafael, que relatou ter ouvido um forte barulho e chegou a perder o equilíbrio.

"Eu vim andando aqui na minha bicicleta e senti aquela lapada [sic]. Eu tomei um susto e quase caí, pois acelerei tentando sair logo lá de perto. Quando eu olhei, vi lá no outro lado, no pé de manga, o corpo de uma pessoa", relatou.

Bombeiros precisaram acionar a Energisa para desligar a energia e conseguir remover o corpo — Foto: Mazinho Rogério/Rede Amazônica Acre

Elissandro era integrante da comunidade indígena Kaxinawá, do município de Jordão, no interior do Acre. Segundo familiares, ele estava em Cruzeiro do Sul há cerca de cinco meses, e estava hospedado na casa de parentes.

O jovem foi ao município para fazer uma perícia após sofrer um acidente envolvendo uma arma de fogo. Segundo o tio-avô, um disparo atingiu a mão de Alessandro. "Ele já veio encaminhado e estava só aguardando e esperando o resultado", relatou José Matheus.

O tio-avô relatou a tristeza da família com a perda do jovem, visto que até a manhã desta quarta, os demais parente ainda não sabiam da morte. "É uma tristeza e muito preocupação para a família, pois o pai, mãe e sobrinhos ainda não ficaram sabendo estamos sofrendo muito", completou José Matheus.

O corpo de Alessandro foi encaminhado ao Instituto Médico Legal (IML) de Cruzeiro do Sul para os procedimentos legais antes de ser liberado à família.

Ainda conforme o subtenente Neri, em caso de choque elétrico, a primeira é manter a calma e jamais tocar na vítima enquanto ela estiver em contato com a fiação ou o aparelho energizado.

Além disso, ele alerta que tentar puxar a pessoa com as mãos ou usar objetos metálicos e molhados pode fazer com que o socorrista também receba a descarga elétrica, tornando-se uma segunda vítima. A orientação imediata é desligar o disjuntor ou a chave geral de energia.

Somente após interromper a eletricidade é seguro se aproximar para avaliar a consciência e a respiração da vítima. Caso ela não esteja respirando, o socorro especializado deve ser acionado imediatamente pelo Samu (192) ou Corpo de Bombeiros (193).

O coordenador reforça que a avaliação médica é indispensável mesmo se a pessoa parecer bem, especialmente se houver desmaio, queimaduras, dor no peito ou dificuldades respiratórias. Para evitar que tais acidentes aconteçam, o subtenente listou dicas essenciais de prevenção para o dia a dia.

articles.title:
Internada em centro de cuidados paliativos, mulher ensina receita de família para equipe do hospital e prato é servido a funcionários e pacientes
 | G1
articles.standfirst: Receita afetiva foi preparada pela equipe de nutrição para pacientes, acompanhantes e funcionários. Após mais de 70 dias internada, Edina Cristina Francisco voltou para casa com acompanhamento médico.
articles.summary: Receita afetiva foi preparada pela equipe de nutrição para pacientes, acompanhantes e funcionários. Após mais de 70 dias internada, Edina Cristina Francisco voltou para casa.
articles.body:
Aos 51 anos, Edina Cristina Francisco encontrou no sabor de uma receita de família um momento de acolhimento durante o tratamento contra um câncer de pele. Internada na unidade de cuidados paliativos do Hospital Erasto Gaertner, em Curitiba , ela ensinou para a equipe de nutrição como preparar um delicioso salpicão. O prato foi feito para pacientes, acompanhantes e funcionários e virou sucesso na unidade. Veja a receita no fim da reportagem .

A iniciativa também ajudou a aproximar Edina de casa em um período delicado, marcado por uma longa internação e pela recuperação de uma cirurgia.

“Eu achei que eles iam fazer só ali, mas, dessa vez, fizeram para o hospital inteiro, para os funcionários, médicos, pacientes e acompanhantes. [...] Não imaginava que ia dar tanta repercussão, porque é um prato simples, e foi muito falado, muito comentado. Cada enfermeiro que chegava ao quarto falava que também ia fazer em casa no fim de semana. Então, fiquei muito surpresa”, lembrou Edina.

A paciente descobriu o melanoma, um tipo de câncer de pele, em setembro de 2024, após perceber uma lesão no calcanhar. A doença avançou e atingiu o intestino. Depois de passar por três cirurgias e ficar 30 dias internada no Hospital Erasto Gaertner, ela foi transferida, em 15 de julho, para o hospice, onde permaneceu por 43 dias.

🔎 Hospice é um serviço especializado no atendimento a pacientes com doenças graves ou avançadas, com foco no conforto, no controle dos sintomas e na qualidade de vida. O hospice onde Edina está internada é o único do Paraná e tem 25 leitos.

Durante a internação, a paciente sentia dificuldades com a comida do hospital e a equipe decidiu dar a ela a oportunidade de escolher o que gostaria de comer.

Em uma conversa com a mãe dela, surgiu a ideia do salpicão, receita que Edina costumava preparar em reuniões de família. Ela escreveu o modo de preparo à mão e entregou à nutricionista. A equipe de nutrição e cozinha do hospital preparou o prato para todos, servindo em canudinhos.

“Eu costumo fazer ele com batata palha, faço numa travessa, quando tem reunião de família. Mas lá no hospital a gente teve a ideia de colocar no canudinho e ficou muito bom”, disse a paciente.

Edina Cristina Francisco segura o salpicão preparado pela equipe do hospice a partir de sua receita de família — Foto: Hospital Erasto Gaertner

O médico de cuidados paliativos Luiz Sérgio Batista Segundo explica que o objetivo do hospice é oferecer conforto e qualidade de vida a pacientes com doenças graves, mesmo quando não há possibilidade de reverter o quadro clínico.

“Talvez a importância do hospice, em um caso como este, seja oferecer o que ela precisa, no momento em que precisa”, afirma o médico.

Salpicão da Edina preparado pela equipe do hospice a partir de sua receita de família — Foto: Hospital Erasto Gaertner

No caso de Edina, ela chegou à unidade após uma cirurgia abdominal de grande porte, com complicações e dificuldades para se recuperar. A equipe trabalhou no controle dos sintomas, na adaptação da bolsa de colostomia e na recuperação da mobilidade, com fisioterapia e acompanhamento nutricional e psicológico.

Ainda conforme o médico, a equipe de nutrição teve um papel importante ao ouvir Edina e entender o significado afetivo da receita. Como ela não podia ir para casa preparar o salpicão, os profissionais levaram um pouco do ambiente familiar para dentro do hospice.

"Já que ela não consegue ir para casa fazer, a gente traz a casa dela o mais perto possível aqui. Fez com que ela se sentisse mais animada", disse o médico.

Edina destaca a atenção dos profissionais durante os 43 dias de internação. Ela também percebeu diferenças em relação ao hospital onde estava antes, como a possibilidade de descansar em um ambiente mais tranquilo e receber a visita de familiares.

“Eu me senti bem acolhida mesmo. Foi muito especial o tempo que passei lá”, relata.

Edina Cristina Francisco — Foto: Hospital Erasto Gaertner

Após mais de 70 dias internada, Edina recebeu alta e voltou para casa , onde continua sendo acompanhada pela equipe do hospice. O atendimento inclui visitas de profissionais de saúde, como médicos, enfermeiros, nutricionistas e psicólogos, além de contatos por telefone para acompanhar a recuperação.

A paciente conta que o suporte é importante, principalmente para lidar com os cuidados com a bolsa de colostomia. Segundo ela, a equipe mantém contato frequente para saber como está a adaptação em casa.

O Paraná tem apenas um hospice, com 25 leitos, segundo o Atlas Brasileiro de Cuidados Paliativos 2025, da Academia Nacional de Cuidados Paliativos (ANCP). O levantamento identifica 15 hospices em todo o Brasil, somando 444 leitos.

Apesar de o número de serviços de cuidados paliativos ter praticamente dobrado no país em três anos, passando de 234 programas em 2022 para 423 em 2025, a oferta ainda é distribuída de maneira desigual.

A região Sudeste concentra 40% dos programas, enquanto o Norte tem apenas 3%. Além disso, 65% dos serviços estão nas capitais.

Segundo a ANCP, mais de 625 mil brasileiros precisam de cuidados paliativos todos os anos.

Para o médico paliativista Douglas Crispim, o crescimento da rede representa um avanço importante, mas propõe uma nova etapa para os cuidados paliativos no Brasil.

"O país conseguiu ampliar o número de serviços, mas agora o desafio é consolidar programas estruturados, capazes de oferecer atendimento seguro, integrado e baseado em evidências. Não basta existir um serviço de cuidados paliativos; precisa estar organizado, atuar de forma multiprofissional e fazer parte da estratégia assistencial do hospital", ressalta.

Misture bem todos os ingredientes em uma tigela. Em seguida, coloque a mistura nos canudinhos e sirva.

articles.title: Bebê morre após grávida ir de moto ao hospital por falta de ambulância | G1
articles.standfirst: O Ministério Público de Mato Grosso do Sul investiga atendimento a gestantes após morte de bebê por falta de socorro.
articles.summary: O Ministério Público de Mato Grosso do Sul investiga atendimento a gestantes após morte de bebê por falta de socorro.
articles.body:
Gestante não teve atendimento telefônico. — Foto: Divulgação

A morte de uma recém-nascida em maio deste ano levou o Ministério Público de Mato Grosso do Sul (MPMS) a apurar as condições da assistência materno-infantil em Sete Quedas (MS). O caso ocorreu no Hospital Municipal da cidade e levantou questionamentos sobre o atendimento de urgência à gestante e a estrutura disponível para partos de alta complexidade.

Segundo informações que constam no procedimento, a gestante teria procurado transporte de emergência por telefone, mas não conseguiu atendimento. Sem ambulância, ela precisou seguir de motocicleta até o hospital.

No local, a unidade não tinha estrutura cirúrgica para realizar uma cesariana. A gestante apresentava um parto pélvico, situação em que o bebê está com os pés ou as nádegas voltados para baixo, em vez da cabeça. O procedimento administrativo busca esclarecer as condições de atendimento prestadas antes e durante o parto.

A apuração também vai verificar se os protocolos de acompanhamento pré-natal foram cumpridos na atenção básica. Outro ponto analisado é o funcionamento do telefone usado para acionar ambulâncias de urgência no município.

Após o caso, a 1ª Promotoria de Justiça de Sete Quedas instaurou um procedimento administrativo para fiscalizar a assistência materno-infantil oferecida pela rede pública. A medida busca reunir informações técnicas sobre o atendimento e identificar eventuais falhas na estrutura ou nos serviços oferecidos às gestantes.

O MPMS requisitou à Secretaria Municipal de Saúde e à direção do Hospital Municipal esclarecimentos técnicos e cópias dos protocolos de atendimento. Os órgãos têm prazo de 15 dias para apresentar as informações solicitadas.

O Conselho Regional de Medicina de Mato Grosso do Sul (CRM/MS) e o Conselho Regional de Enfermagem de Mato Grosso do Sul (Coren/MS) também receberam ofícios para ciência do caso e adoção das medidas que considerarem necessárias dentro de suas áreas de fiscalização.

A apuração do MPMS tem caráter investigativo. Neste momento, o procedimento busca esclarecer as circunstâncias do atendimento e verificar se houve falhas na assistência prestada à gestante e à recém-nascida.

articles.title: Jovem morre por complicações de apendicite após buscar ajuda 3 vezes | G1
articles.standfirst: Secretaria Municipal de Saúde abriu sindicância para apurar o atendimento prestado a estudante de 18 anos no Hospital Municipal Pedro II, em Santa Cruz. Caso é investigado pela Polícia Civil.
articles.summary: João Victor Azeredo, de 18 anos, morreu no último sábado (3) após complicações de apendicite. A família acusa o Hospital Municipal Pedro II de negligência médica.
articles.body:
A família de João Victor Azeredo, de 18 anos, acusa médicos do Hospital Municipal Pedro II, em Santa Cruz, na Zona Oeste do Rio, de negligência no atendimento que antecedeu a morte do estudante de Educação Física. Ele morreu no último sábado (3), após passar 15 dias internado na unidade.

Segundo os parentes, João Victor procurou o hospital pela primeira vez no dia 16 de setembro com fortes dores abdominais. A família afirma que ele permaneceu internado por cerca de 12 horas e realizou duas tomografias, mas não recebeu um diagnóstico conclusivo.

De acordo com o pai dele, Bruno Azeredo, houve divergência entre médicos sobre a necessidade de uma cirurgia.

"Entra em atrito dois cirurgiões que viram o laudo da tomografia. Um diz que é caso cirúrgico e outro diz que não vai operar", afirmou Bruno Azeredo, pai do jovem.

Ainda segundo a família, o jovem foi medicado e recebeu alta com a orientação de tratar em casa um quadro de gastroenterite.

"Meu filho não tinha nenhuma doença. Meu filho chegou andando aqui nesse hospital, andando, falando, conversando. E foi negligenciado nesse hospital", disse o pai de João Victor.

As dores continuaram, e João Victor voltou ao hospital poucas horas depois, acompanhado do pai. Ainda de acordo com os parentes, ele recebeu morfina e foi liberado novamente.

No dia 18 de setembro, a família retornou pela terceira vez à unidade. Segundo o relato dos parentes, apenas nesse momento os médicos diagnosticaram uma apendicite. A família afirma que o apêndice já havia se rompido e que o abdômen estava infeccionado.

O jovem passou por uma cirurgia de emergência. Após 15 dias de internação, morreu no hospital.

O pai do estudante defende que o desfecho poderia ter sido evitado caso a cirurgia tivesse sido realizada logo no primeiro atendimento. A família pede uma apuração rigorosa do caso.

"Meu filho não escolheu estar aqui. Eles estudaram para estar aqui. Foi negligência pura com o meu filho. Se tivessem operado o meu filho no primeiro dia, ele estaria bem. Eles deram um laudo errado. Eles erraram", afirmou.

Jovem de 18 anos morre por complicações de apendicite após buscar atendimento três vezes — Foto: Reprodução

Em nota, a Secretaria Municipal de Saúde informou que abriu uma sindicância para apurar os detalhes do atendimento prestado ao paciente.

A direção do Hospital Municipal Pedro II afirmou que tem prestado todas as informações à família e que permanece à disposição para fornecer esclarecimentos sobre o caso.

O caso foi registrado na 36ªDP (Santa Cruz), que investiga o caso.

articles.title: O que se sabe sobre a morte da Rainha de Rodeio atingida por raio  | G1
articles.standfirst: Ana Beatriz Araújo, de 22 anos, era rainha do rodeio de Almas (TO). Ela chegou a ser reanimada depois de perder os batimentos cardíacos, mas não resistiu.
articles.summary: Ana Beatriz Araújo, de 22 anos, era rainha do rodeio de Almas (TO). Ela chegou a ser reanimada depois de perder os batimentos cardíacos, mas não resistiu.
articles.body:
A morte da rainha de rodeio Ana Beatriz Araújo, de 22 anos , após ser atingida por uma descarga elétrica durante uma chuva leve em Almas , no sudeste do Tocantins, surpreendeu amigos e familiares. Além dela, uma sobrinha de 8 anos também foi atingida pela descarga elétrica.

Segundo a família, a criança chegou a ficar sem sentir as pernas , foi internada para observação e recebeu alta após exames. A Secretaria da Segurança Pública disse que caso segue sob apuração da 100ª Delegacia de Polícia de Almas.

Ana havia completado 22 anos no dia 26 de setembro, uma semana antes do acidente. Ela foi sepultada na segunda-feira (5), mesma data em que a irmã, Lana Letícia, completou 24 anos.

Rainha de Rodeio Ana Beatriz Araújo, de 22 anos, morreu após ser atingida por um raio, em Almas (TO) — Foto: Divulgação/ Sindicato Rural de Almas

Ana Beatriz e a sobrinha foram atingidas por uma descarga elétrica causada por um raio na tarde de sábado (3), em Almas. Segundo familiares, Ana estava penteando o cabelo da sobrinha durante uma chuva considerada leve quando o raio atingiu o local. As duas caíram no chão após a descarga elétrica.

O acidente aconteceu em uma pequena área coberta localizada nos fundos da residência da família, na zona urbana de Almas. No local havia um tanque para lavar roupas e diversas árvores no quintal. Imagens gravadas após o ocorrido mostram a estrutura onde as vítimas estavam no momento da descarga elétrica.

De acordo com familiares, o sábado começou nublado e a chuva começou durante a tarde. Eles afirmaram que o tempo não aparentava oferecer risco e que a precipitação era fraca quando ocorreu a descarga elétrica.

A menina de 8 anos foi atingida pela descarga elétrica. Segundo a família, ela acordou após o acidente, mas ficou algumas horas sem sentir as pernas . A criança foi levada ao Hospital Regional de Dianópolis, onde passou por exames, permaneceu internada em observação e recebeu alta no dia seguinte. A dormência desapareceu e, conforme os parentes, ela está bem.

Conhecida como "Aninha", Ana Beatriz Araújo tinha 22 anos e havia sido eleita rainha de rodeio da 27ª edição da ExpoAlmas 2026. Ela havia ingressado recentemente no curso de Fisioterapia e era mãe de um menino. Familiares e pessoas próximas relatam que ela conciliava os estudos com os cuidados da família.

articles.body:
Imagens de uma câmera de segurança mostra a sequência que terminou com um micro-ônibus usado no transporte escolar dentro de um rio em Cipotânea , na Zona da Mata mineira. O acidente aconteceu na tarde da segunda-feira (5), na Travessa Capitão Gomes.

Não havia alunos no veículo , e o motorista sofreu ferimentos leves.

O vídeo mostra o veículo subindo a rua e, segundos depois, retornando de ré. Na descida, atinge uma motocicleta e, em seguida, a estrutura de proteção de uma ponte. Com o impacto, a proteção é rompida, e o veículo cai no leito do rio. Assista acima.

Segundo o relato do motorista à PM, ele percebeu um problema no sistema de freios quando parou no cruzamento. O coletivo começou a descer e, mesmo tentando controlar o micro-ônibus, o condutor não conseguiu evitar a queda.

Apesar de o veículo fazer parte da frota de transporte escolar da Prefeitura de Cipotânea, nenhum aluno estava no micro-ônibus no momento do acidente.

O motorista, de 33 anos, era o único ocupante. Ele foi retirado do veículo com ajuda de moradores e levado ao Hospital Municipal São Caetano, com ferimentos leves. Depois, recebeu alta.

A Prefeitura informou que o micro-ônibus estava com vistoria, manutenção e documentação em dia. O veículo foi retirado do rio ainda na segunda-feira, e a administração municipal informou que apura as circunstâncias do acidente. A perícia esteve fazendo levantamentos no local.

Um carro bateu em um poste na Avenida Eliseu de Almeida, na altura do número 496, no bairro Butantã, na Zona Oeste de São Paulo , às 16h54 desta quarta-feira (7). Três pessoas ficaram feridas.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, uma das vítimas estava em estado grave e foi transportada pelo helicóptero Águia-18 ao Hospital das Clínicas (HC). As outras duas vítimas foram levadas pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) ao Hospital Universitário (HU).

articles.summary: Batida aconteceu na BR-060, entre uma van que retornava de Campo Grande para Bela Vista e uma SUV; oito pessoas já receberam alta.
articles.body:
Carro envolvido em acidente na BR-060 ficou destruído. — Foto: Prefeitura de Bela Vista

Quatro vítimas da batida envolvendo uma van que transportava pacientes de hemodiálise e uma SUV , ocorrida nesta terça-feira (6), na BR-060, continuam internadas. Três delas estão na Santa Casa de Campo Grande, onde passam por exames complementares. A quarta vítima está internada no Hospital São Vicente de Paula, em Bela Vista .

Outras oito vítimas já receberam alta, conforme a Prefeitura de Bela Vista. Inicialmente, o município havia informado que a van transportava 17 pessoas. Nesta quarta-feira (8), porém, a prefeitura corrigiu o número e informou que havia 13 pessoas no veículo. Dessas, 12 ficaram feridas e precisaram ser encaminhadas para unidades de saúde.

Entre os feridos estava o motorista da van. Apesar de ter sofrido apenas ferimentos leves, ele permaneceu no local e ajudou a prestar assistência aos pacientes que estavam no veículo, segundo a Prefeitura de Bela Vista. Ele foi o último a deixar o local do acidente, acompanhado de outro paciente que não se feriu.

Não há confirmação sobre o estado de saúde do motorista do outro veículo.

A van retornava de Campo Grande, onde os pacientes haviam realizado o tratamento de hemodiálise, e seguia para Bela Vista.

Segundo a Prefeitura de Bela Vista, a SUV que colidiu com a van estaria fugindo da polícia. Durante uma manobra, o motorista teria atingido o veículo que transportava os pacientes.

Equipes da Secretaria Municipal de Saúde acompanham a situação e mantêm contato com as unidades hospitalares. De acordo com a prefeitura, os profissionais também estão à disposição dos pacientes e dos familiares para prestar assistência.

articles.title: New ‘Blue Zone’ on the map? THIS tiny Italian village offers clues to women’s longevity
articles.summary: In the rugged hills of Sardinia, there’s a small village called Bolotana that’s been catching the eyes of longevity researchers worldwide.
articles.body: In the rugged hills of Sardinia, there’s a small village called Bolotana that’s been catching the eyes of longevity researchers worldwide. Bolotana, home to only about 2,300 people, has emerged as a potential new “Blue Zone”: a term usually reserved for places where people show exceptional survival into old age. This isn’t just another picturesque Italian outpost; something is happening here that’s got scientists digging through dusty birth records, trying to figure out why women in this community seem to live longer, healthier lives than just about anyone else.The numbers are striking. According to research published in Frontiers in Aging, in Bolotana, researchers found that roughly 14% (13.8%, to be precise) of women who make it to 70 can expect to see 100 candles on their birthday cake. To put that in perspective, only about 3.5% of 70-year-old women in Italy and the US reach the century mark, which means women in Bolotana are nearly four times as likely to hit triple digits. On average, a woman in Bolotana who turns 70 should plan for another two decades.Where is Bolotana and why is it special?Bolotana sits in the mountainous Marghine area of Sardinia, an Italian island already famous for exceptional longevity. Sardinia's original Blue Zone consists of a cluster of mountain villages where researchers have documented unusually high numbers of long-lived people, particularly men. Bolotana is outside that original cluster.The village first caught researchers' attention because of its unusually high concentration of centenarians. In 2024, six people aged 100 or older were living there, which is a prevalence estimated to be roughly 11 times that of the US.Looking back at age-old records of BolotanaNow, of course, in a tiny town, absolute numbers can be a bit misleading, so the researchers took pains to dig deeper, reconstructing entire population cohorts, verifying every claim. No easy task, but Bolotana’s thorough archives make it possible, lending a rare layer of credibility to the findings.And it turns out, it’s not just a statistical blip either. Scientists, led by teams publishing in journals like Frontiers in Aging, have painstakingly tracked down old municipal files, church baptismal ledgers, and family records. They documented 38 people who reached at least 100 among 3,060 people born in Bolotana between 1900 and 1925. According to the University of Illinois Chicago, every centenarian identified in the study had an official birth record.Sure, it's not the first time Sardinia has drawn international attention for healthy aging (the island is already famous for its “Blue Zone” villages where men live an unusually long time), but Bolotana is outside the original cluster. For some reason, the women here are far and away the real standouts.Why are women in Bolotana living so long?The honest answer: nobody’s entirely sure yet. There’s no magic recipe, no singular miracle olive oil or secret daily ritual. What the researchers know is that village life here checks off nearly every box that scientists think might help people reach old age: people walk everywhere, weaving up and down steep, winding lanes rather than driving; families live close to each other; social connections seem strong, with neighbors popping in and out of each other’s homes. Most of the food comes from around the region, with plenty of local olive oil and produce. But, crucially, none of these habits stand out as the “smoking gun,” and it’s too early to say whether copying Bolotana’s lifestyle can guarantee similar results elsewhere.For the study, the researchers, in fact, analyzed two key measures: life expectancy at age 70 and the probability of surviving from 70 to 100. For women in Bolotana, the estimated life expectancy at 70 was 20.85 additional years. Their estimated probability of reaching 100 was 13.83%.Men also showed impressive longevity, with an estimated 16.02 additional years at age 70 and a 4.92% probability of reaching 100. But the female advantage was much more pronounced.According to researchers, it makes Bolotana particularly unusual because women generally live longer than men worldwide, but the scale of the difference here is striking. Per S. Jay Olshansky, a senior author of the study, the researchers believe Bolotana may have one of the longest-lived female populations in the world.Is Bolotana really a new Blue Zone?However, despite all the potential ingredients for the prestigious status, the study’s authors are careful to call Bolotana a “candidate Blue Zone,” not a full-fledged member of the world’s legendary longevity hotspots (like Okinawa or Ikaria).Why so?When they dove into different time periods (say, comparing 2015–2019 against 2021–2025), the percentage of women reaching 100 jumped dramatically in recent years. Earlier data showed much lower average numbers. That kind of fluctuation means scientists can’t just call Bolotana the world’s new capital for healthy aging. There’s more work to do, more years to observe, more records to comb through.And yet, there’s something deeply compelling about this place and its women. If you reach 70 in Bolotana, statistics suggest you’ll almost certainly outpace your global peers, and women hold the clear advantage. Here, the gap between male and female longevity, already present in most countries, is much wider.What could the rest of us learn from Bolotana?Researchers are looking at everything from genetics to how people move, eat, and relate to each other. Sure, it’s possible that the secret eventually comes down to something simple: walking a lot, eating real food, talking to people every day, and growing old not in isolation but in a tight-knit web of family and friends. Maybe that’s not glamorous enough to launch a wellness trend, but beneath the viral diets and supplements, that’s probably where the real story lives.As of now, Bolotana remains a sort of mystery waiting to be unraveled: a tiny village with quiet streets, old women doing what they’ve always done, living longer than anyone expected. And if there’s a secret, it’s probably hidden not in a pill, but in the ordinary, everyday rhythms that bind people to each other and to this windswept corner of Sardinia.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: Los entrenadores personales coinciden: “A partir de los 70 años, caminar entre 20 y 30 minutos cinco veces por semana es suficiente para obtener beneficios reales”
articles.standfirst: La idea de hacer 10.000 pasos deja de ser considerada por la ciencia
articles.summary: La idea de hacer 10.000 pasos deja de ser considerada por la ciencia
articles.body: Durante años, la meta de los 10.000 pasos diarios se ha vendido como el estándar mínimo de la salud física, muy recomendado para personas mayores de 60 años que ya no pueden realizar actividades físicas más fuertes. Sin embargo, la ciencia y la medicina preventiva desmienten la necesidad de alcanzar esa cifra, especialmente al superar la barrera de los 65 años. Para la población sénior, la pauta médica actual ya no se mide en pasos, sino en minutos de movimiento continuo. La Organización Mundial de la Salud y los especialistas coinciden en que lo idóneo es pasear unos 30 minutos al día a ritmo moderado, sumando unos 150 minutos a la semana. De hecho, varios estudios confirman que hacer entre 6.000 y 7.000 pasos diarios reduce de forma drástica la mortalidad cardiovascular y protege la salud neurológica. El secreto sería ajustar el esfuerzo a las capacidades de cada persona. Como explica el preparador físico Rafael Hidalgo: "Para empezar, no hace falta hacer grandes tiempos. Con 20 a 30 minutos ya se obtienen beneficios a nivel cardiovascular, movilidad y bienestar general. A partir de ahí, se puede progresar hacia los 40-60 minutos, siempre adaptando la intensidad", explicó en declaraciones a la revista Semana. "Es prioritario llevar un ritmo ágil que active la circulación sin llegar al agotamiento ni comprometer las articulaciones. Lo crucial a esta edad no es batir récords, sino consolidar un hábito sostenible que garantice la autonomía funcional y mantenga la masa muscular", apuntó. Es decir, tratar de compensar una semana sedentaria con caminatas más largas y duras en el fin de semana es un error. Lo ideal es un paseo diario de 30 minutos a paso ligero, sobre todo a partir de la edad mencionada.

articles.title: Shingles rates fall off a cliff among some Americans as researchers reveal likely reason
articles.summary: Epic Research analyzed 85 million health records and found shingles rates dropped 62% among younger adults eligible for childhood chickenpox vaccination.
articles.body: Shingles rates have dropped sharply among younger U.S. adults, as the first generation eligible for routine childhood chickenpox vaccination is now in their late 20s. That’s according to a major study led by Epic Research, which analyzed the electronic health records of more than 85 million adults. The biggest drop was between people born from 1991 to 1995 and those born from 1996 to 2000. FDA APPROVES FIRST-EVER MRNA FLU VACCINE FOR MILLIONS OF OLDER AMERICANS "Shingles is caused by a virus that is harbored in the peripheral nerves — varicella-zoster, the same virus that causes chickenpox — which can remain dormant and later reactivate, particularly during stress or other decreased immune responses, resulting in a shingles risk," Dr. Marc Siegel, Fox News senior medical analyst, told Fox News Digital. About 46 out of every 10,000 people in the older group were diagnosed with shingles, compared with just 17 out of every 10,000 in the younger group — a 62% decrease. The study period was between January 2017 and June 2026, with the findings published on Oct. 2, 2026. CANCER VACCINE PREVENTS DEADLY MELANOMA FROM RETURNING OR SPREADING IN LANDMARK TRIAL Overall, shingles was found to be much more common in older adults. About 182 out of every 10,000 people born between 1968 and 1975 were diagnosed with the condition, compared with just seven out of every 10,000 born between 2006 and 2008. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER "Shingles diagnoses rise steeply with age, but the newer signal is a sharp drop that begins with people who were eligible for the childhood chickenpox vaccine in the mid-1990s," study author Kersten Bartelt, a research clinician in Verona, Wisconsin, told Fox News Digital. "This is the pattern we would expect if childhood chickenpox vaccination lowers the risk of developing shingles later in life." If the trend continues as vaccinated groups grow older, it would suggest that childhood chickenpox vaccination could offer a lasting benefit in reducing shingles, "which is something continued follow-up and research will clarify," Bartelt added. Siegel agreed that this data aligns with previous research showing that by preventing the initial infection via the chickenpox vaccine ("or causing a very mild version of a live virus vaccine") the risk of shingles is significantly reduced. "This is the pattern we would expect if childhood chickenpox vaccination lowers the risk of developing shingles later in life." He noted that the vaccine uses a weakened form of the virus, which is much less likely to reactivate later in life and cause shingles. There were some limitations of the study, including that the researchers did not determine whether individual patients had actually received the varicella vaccination during childhood. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "This is a descriptive, observational study, so it shows associations rather than cause and effect," Bartelt said. Healthcare disruption due to the COVID pandemic in 2020-2021 could have also affected diagnosis rates and skewed the results, the researchers noted. Future studies are needed to confirm a link between childhood vaccination histories and long-term shingles outcomes. "People should continue to follow established vaccine recommendations and talk with their clinician about the shingles vaccine when they're eligible," Bartelt advised. "It's also a reminder that shingles can occur in younger adults, so anyone with a painful, blistering rash should seek timely evaluation." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ While people who received the chickenpox vaccine have a lower risk of developing shingles, Siegel said he still recommends that eligible people get the shingles vaccine to further reduce that risk. articles.title: This Is the First Question a Therapist Asks When Diagnosing Depression. Here’s Why
articles.summary: Depression can be caused by a range of factors, from family history to stressful events and lifestyle habits.
articles.body: Depression can be caused by a range of factors, from family history to stressful events and lifestyle habits. That’s psychotherapist Niro Feliciano has a go-to question when talking to a new client about potential signs of the mental health condition. Mental Health Tip of the Day: Think About Your Screen Time When Assessing Yourself for Depression “When I’d have a client come in and they’d say, ‘I don’t feel motivated to do the things that I like to do, that I normally do to start a new habit,’ I would automatically begin to assess them for depression,” Feliciano explains. “And now the first thing I ask is, ‘Let’s talk about your screen time.’” That’s because of the high levels of the “feel-good hormone” dopamine that devices like smartphones provide, she says, which can make it easier to do other tasks, especially if they’re boring or unrewarding at the beginning. Why It Matters Research has found that high amounts of screen time can be a predictor for depression symptoms. It’s a phenomenon that’s especially concerning for preteens and adolescents, experts say. Some studies have indicated that the connection may be that more screen time leads less physical activity (which has been linked to better mental health), poor sleep quality and social challenges. How to Get Started If you’re struggling with depression symptoms, it’s recommended to see a mental healthcare provider, such as a therapist or psychiatrist. (If you are in immediate crisis, the 988 National Suicide & Crisis Hotline is Available.) For most people, depression can be treatable with a combination of talk therapy, medications and lifestyle changes, according to Mayo Clinic. Looking to cut back on your screen time specifically? Try Feliciano’s 30-day plan to improve your attention span, which involves a lot less time on your phone.
